target.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling an embedded Lobster workflow could leave default child processes running, allow later pipeline stages to execute, or preserve the cancelled run as resumable input work. In the Gmail workflow, a cancelled search could finish after the parent stopped and continue into the side-effecting `gog.gmail.send` stage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pipeline runtime now checks its `AbortSignal` before execution, after commands return, between stages, while collecting output, and before turning an input suspension into resumable state. Finalization also checks around resume-state and approval-index persistence, cleaning newly created artifacts if cancellation wins that race. Resumed pipeline cancellation also invalidates the prior resume state so partially completed side effects cannot be replayed with the old token or approval ID. Process-backed default commands that previously ignored cancellation (`gog.gmail.search`, `gog.gmail.send`, and the legacy GitHub PR monitor workflow) now pass the same signal to their child process; Gmail send also rechecks cancellation before each draft.

This is scoped to process-backed paths reachable from the default embedded runtime. Existing signal-aware `exec`, `openclaw.agent`, and workflow-file shell paths are unchanged; optional SDK-only recipes and HTTP adapter request cancellation are outside this patch.

## User Impact

Cancelling a parent run now promptly stops the affected Lobster child process and prevents later process-backed stages from starting. In particular, a cancelled Gmail workflow no longer continues toward sending email after the parent has stopped.

## Evidence

Stock-main regression proof failed as expected:

- Gmail search pipeline: did not settle within 500ms and continued for about 2.58s.
- In-flight Gmail send: did not settle within 500ms and continued for about 1.29s.
- Pipeline stage boundary: the post-cancellation side-effect stage still ran.
- Default GitHub monitor subprocess: continued for about 1.31s after abort.
- Terminal input suspension race: returned `needs_input` and persisted resume state after the parent signal was already aborted.
- Finalization persistence race: input and approval suspensions could write resumable state after `runPipeline()` returned but before the tool envelope was finalized.

Live embedded-runtime proof after the fix:

```text
{
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledWithin100msAfterAbort": true,
  "childStillRunningAfterAbort": false,
  "searchTerminated": true,
  "searchCompletedMarker": null,
  "sendStartedAfterAbort": false,
  "sendCompletedMarker": null,
  "settledAfterAbortMs": 1,
  "outcome": "resolved_error_envelope",
  "errorType": "runtime_error"
}
```

Validation:

- `pnpm test` — 317/317 tests passed, including eight cancellation regressions.
- `pnpm format:check` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig tsconfig.json bin src test` — passed (four pre-existing warnings outside this diff).
- `pnpm typecheck` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
